title: Divisibility by 3 OQ-03-OQ-02: Base-Parametric Digital Roots
description: Records the Lean base-parametric digital-root and divisibility rules for Nat.digits in arbitrary bases.

problemStatement.formal: Define `digitalRootBase b n` and prove congruence/divisibility rules modulo b - 1 for base-b digit sums.
problemStatement.plain: Generalizes the decimal digital-root rule to any base b, including reusable divisibility tests for factors of b - 1.
whyMatters: It turns the familiar divisibility-by-3 rule into a base-independent theorem.
The proof uses Mathlib digit-sum congruence lemmas instead of ad hoc decimal arithmetic.
Concrete octal, hexadecimal, and base-7 checks make the theorem computationally testable.

proven: `digitSum_mod_base_pred` and `congruence` prove the digit-sum congruence modulo b - 1.
`digitalRootBase_range`, `digitalRootBase_single`, and `digitalRootBase_idempotent` prove the expected root behavior.
`hex_div15`, `oct_div7`, and the concrete root examples check non-decimal bases.
`DivisibilityBy3OQ03OQ02.lean` is recorded with 0 axioms and 0 sorries.
open: The file gives divisibility rules for factors of b - 1, not a full catalogue of all digit tests for arbitrary moduli.
knownResults.goal: Expose the completed base-parametric digital-root formalization and its verified divisibility rules.

source.proofTitle: Efficient Digital Root Computation via Modular Arithmetic

problemStatement.formal: For base b >= 3, formalize digitalRootBase b n and its congruence to n modulo b - 1 using Nat.digits b n.
problemStatement.plain: Generalize the familiar base-10 digit-sum divisibility rule to arbitrary bases by proving that the digital root tracks residues modulo b - 1.
whyMatters: The result turns a base-specific divisibility trick into reusable modular-arithmetic infrastructure.
It connects Lean's digit-list API to practical divisibility tests in bases such as 8, 10, and 16.

proven: digitalRootBase defines the base-b digital root as 0 at n = 0 and 1 + (n - 1) % (b - 1) otherwise.
digitSum_mod_base_pred and congruence relate digit sums and digital roots to n modulo b - 1.
digitalRootBase_range, digitalRootBase_single, and digitalRootBase_idempotent prove range and stability properties.
div_pred_iff_div_digitSum proves the divisibility rule by b - 1 using the digit sum.
factor_div_rule generalizes the rule to any factor d of b - 1.
base10_eq_OQ03_formula plus base 16, base 8, and base 7 examples connect the general theorem to concrete computations.
knownResults.goal: Expose the completed base-parametrized digital-root theorem family without changing the underlying proof artifacts.
